Our PostgreSQL 18 service has concurrent workers that read a cross-row business invariant and then update different rows. The team proposes Repeatable Read because a stable snapshot and absence of phantom rows should make the combined decisions equivalent to serial execution. If a transaction fails for a serialization reason, the proposed recovery retries only the failed SQL statement, expecting PostgreSQL to replay the earlier decision logic automatically. A generic retry wrapper would also retry every unique-key violation without inspecting its cause.

Decide whether this isolation/recovery design is sufficient and recommend the narrow changes that matter for correctness. Separate PostgreSQL's implementation from the SQL standard's minimum guarantees. Explain who owns retrying, the appropriate retry unit, and whether unique violations belong in an unconditional retry bucket. Product also wants a documented promise that every operation will commit within at most three attempts under contention; can we make it?

- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/mvcc.html

5. Maybe https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html — actually it's "serialization-failure-handling"? The page is titled "Serialization Failure Handling" at https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html? Let me check. In PostgreSQL docs, Chapter 13.2.3? Actually, "Serialization Failure Handling" is a subsection of Chapter 13 (Concurrency Control): https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html. Yes.

Also the protocol / SQL standard distinction: PostgreSQL docs note "the SQL standard defines four levels... Read Uncommitted... Repeatable Read... In PostgreSQL, Repeatable Read is implemented as snapshot isolation; serialization anomalies are possible".

Also unique constraint doc: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-constraints.html#DDL-CONSTRAINTS-UNIQUE-CONSTRAINTS — with default nulls distinct.

Let's do parallel fetches in first call: mvcc.html and transaction-iso.html. Wait, the instruction: "Fetch relevant whole pages and follow their documentation links". Maximum 8 inference calls; tools available calls 1-7. So I can have up to 7 tool calls; final call 8 must be only the answer.

Let me batch: call 1: fetch mvcc.html + transaction-iso.html + mvcc-serialization-failure-handling.html (3 in parallel).

Then call 2: errcodes-appendix.html + ddl-constraints.html (maybe applevel-consistency.html). Then possibly one more for something else.

Key facts:
- Repeatable Read in PostgreSQL uses a snapshot taken at first non-transaction-control statement; it does not prevent lost updates? Actually in PG's Repeatable Read, updating a row that was concurrently modified causes a serialization failure ("could not serialize access due to concurrent update"). But for different rows with cross-row invariant, write skew is possible at RR (snapshot isolation), because different rows written, no conflict detected.
- SQL standard minimum guarantees: the standard defines levels by prohibited phenomena (dirty read, nonrepeatable read, phantom read); RR prohibits dirty/nonrepeatable but allows phantoms; snapshot isolation? Actually the standard's RR is not exactly SI. PostgreSQL's RR is stricter than standard minimum (no phantom reads). Serialization anomalies possible.
- Serialization failure handling: retry the whole transaction.
- Who owns retrying: the application, not Postgres.
- Unique violation (23505) is not a serialization failure; it's a data exception. Doesn't indicate serialization; retrying unconditionally is wrong; often the transaction is fine but statement must be rolled back; concurrent insert conflict is deterministic, not the same as serialization conflict. Unique violation aborts the whole transaction (unlike serialization? No — serialization failure also aborts the transaction). Actually both abort the transaction. Retrying a single statement is not valid: after an error, the transaction is in aborted state, requires ROLLBACK (or ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT). PostgreSQL docs: "If a serialization failure occurs ... the application should retry the transaction" — whole transaction including the decision logic.
- Also SERIALIZABLE is needed for cross-row invariants (write skew prevention); PostgreSQL 9.1+ SSI. Docs say "selecting the appropriate isolation level ... Serializable ... true serializable isolation". Also recommend "If you need to ensure consistency across multiple rows, use Serializable" — check exact text.

Three-attempt commit guarantee: cannot promise; retries can fail indefinitely under contention; docs say "the number of retries needed ... unpredictable". UNVERIFIED/no documented bound. Also 40001 can repeat.

Also error code names: 40001 serialization_failure; 40P01 deadlock_detected; 23505 unique_violation. Chapter 13 "Serialization Failure Handling" says: "the application should retry the transaction, for example: ... It is important to retry the complete transaction, including all logic that decides which SQL statements to issue."

Repeatable Read ... phantom reads are not possible ... stricter..." and "Serializable ... behaves as if transactions executed serially" and "this level is not supported by the SQL standard as a distinct level ... implemented using predicate locking".

Also applevel-consistency: "Some kinds of consistency can only be ensured by ... client-side checks ... SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE". It notes that at lower levels a serialization anomaly might occur.
